rule: lambda = RMS over mini-batches of G_pg / (2 * (1.11 - 1) / 15), two significant figures: on a mini-batch whose tail_3 means all sit at +1.11 the penalty's pull on tail_3's output bias, lambda * 2 * 0.11 / 15, equals the RMS policy-gradient pull on it at the 4,194,304 checkpoint
notes: G_pg is d/d bias[tail_3] of the clipped surrogate at ratio 1 (the first epoch); later epochs move the ratio within the clip and early-stop at approx_kl > 0.045 (target_kl 0.03).

Parameters stay the checkpoint's through all rollouts (no update); the VecNormalize statistics update as in training, and the envs continue their episodes across rollouts (resets only at episode ends).
The penalty touches every actuator, but only means beyond +-1 pay; tail_3 is the only one the 4,194,304 rollouts put there in numbers (see mu beyond fractions in the arms' telemetry).
justification: lambda = 41. The policy-gradient pull on tail_3's mean as a parameter (d clipped-surrogate / d action_net.bias[tail_3], advantages normalised per mini-batch, ratio 1) at the 4,194,304 checkpoint, over 256 mini-batches of 128 from 4 training rollouts: RMS 0.602 (theory 1/(sigma sqrt(B)) = 0.547 at tail_3 sigma 0.162), mean -0.122 +- 0.037 (SEM). The penalty's pull on that bias for a mini-batch whose tail_3 means all sit at +1.11 is lambda * 2 * 0.11 / 15 = lambda * 0.01467; equal to the RMS at lambda = 41.05, rounded to 41 (pull 0.601). Only the ratio matters: the gradient clip (total norm median 53.3 against max_grad_norm 0.5, factor 0.0094) scales both terms alike, and Adam normalises each parameter by its gradient RMS, so a consistent pull of one RMS moves tail_3's bias at roughly 0.7 of the step size per mini-batch.
alternative_not_chosen: Per row instead of per mini-batch (mean |dL/dmu_tail3| per row 0.0257 against lambda * 2 * 0.11 / (15 * 128)) would give lambda about 224, sqrt(B) = 11 times larger; rejected because per-row policy-gradient terms are random in sign and cancel in the parameter gradient while the penalty's add coherently, so it would dominate rather than be comparable.
caveats: [measured] stance5 s42 at 4,194,304 is not parked at +1.11: the deterministic raw mean on pinned window steps is 1.0153 (max 1.0281; beyond +1 on 0.293 of window steps); +1.01..+1.12 was stance4 s42's.

[measured] on the training rollouts tail_3's mean exceeds +1 on 0.037 of rows (by about 0.025-0.03), so the penalty's realized pull at the start is 0.0056, 0.9% of the policy-gradient RMS; the policy-gradient mean (-0.122, descent raises the mean) is about 20 times larger and points the other way.

[inferred] P1 bounds |mu| at 1.0, but the gate counts |cmd| >= 0.99, so a mean held just under 1 is still saturated by the gate's statistic; below 1 the reward is no longer flat (action_saturation ramps from 0.9).

[measured] the deterministic tail numbers swing from one update to the next (control smoke: frac99 0.338 -> 0.557 after 2 updates; P1 smoke 0.267 after 1, 0.575 after 2; the original run 0.338 / 0.171 / 0.565 at 4.19 / 5.24 / 6.29M), so one seed per arm separates P1 from CONTROL only if the difference is large against that spread.
